turns.prompt_text: Alrighty, I have a burn-zo-matic. Small torch. I would like to create a 3D model in SCAD. I am having trouble refilling the gas. I would like to create a nozzle for it, kind of like a funnel that will press down on the butane nozzle.
I'm pretty sure they sell these at Walmart, and they've created their own, but I just like to print one.
turns.response_html:
I totally get the appeal of printing your own—it's a perfect quick project, and dialing in a custom solution is always more satisfying than making a trip to Walmart.

Before diving into the code, just a quick word of caution: pressurized butane can easily escape through the layer lines of a 3D print, which can cause freezing on your fingers or potential fire hazards. To minimize this, you'll want to ensure the walls are completely solid. If you have TPU or a flexible filament on hand, that often creates a much better gas seal than standard PLA or PETG.

Here is a parametric OpenSCAD script for a nozzle adapter. It features a wider flange in the middle so you can easily press down on the butane canister, a bottom cavity to fit tightly over the butane stem, and a top nozzle to depress the pin inside your Bernzomatic torch.

The OpenSCAD Script

// Bernzomatic Butane Refill Adapter
// Note: Measure your specific torch and canister with calipers and adjust these variables!

// --- Variables ---
butane_stem_dia = 4.2;  // Outer diameter of the butane can stem (mm)
torch_valve_dia = 3.0;  // Outer diameter of the adapter tip that goes into the torch (mm)
flange_dia = 15.0;      // Outer diameter of the middle flange for pressing (mm)
total_height = 15.0;    // Overall height of the adapter (mm)
gas_hole_dia = 1.0;     // Internal through-hole for gas flow (mm)

$fn = 100; // Smooth curves for high-resolution printing

// --- Model ---
difference() {
    // Main solid body
    union() {
        // Bottom section (fits over the butane stem)
        cylinder(h = total_height/2, d = butane_stem_dia + 4);
        
        // Middle flange (gives you a surface to press against)
        translate([0, 0, total_height/2 - 2])
            cylinder(h = 4, d = flange_dia);
            
        // Top section (fits into the Bernzomatic torch valve)
        translate([0, 0, total_height/2])
            cylinder(h = total_height/2, d = torch_valve_dia);
    }

    // Internal cutouts for the gas and stems
    // Bottom cavity for the butane stem to sit inside
    translate([0, 0, -0.1])
        cylinder(h = total_height/2 + 0.1, d = butane_stem_dia);
        
    // Tiny through-hole for the gas to travel up into the torch
    translate([0, 0, -0.1])
        cylinder(h = total_height + 0.2, d = gas_hole_dia);
}

Printing Tips

  • Tolerances: Your Bambu Lab A1 should handle these tight circular tolerances beautifully right out of the box, but gas fittings are notoriously finicky. Print a test run, check the fit on both the torch and the canister, and adjust the butane_stem_dia and torch_valve_dia variables by 0.1mm increments until it creates a snug seal.
  • Orientation: Print it vertically, exactly as it renders (with the wider bottom section on the build plate).
  • Settings: Use a fine layer height (0.12mm or 0.08mm) to ensure the top nozzle is as smooth as possible. Set your wall loops/perimeters to a high number (like 10) so the slicer generates the model as a solid block of concentric plastic rings rather than using standard infill patterns. This drastically reduces the chance of gas leaking through the sides.
